item.title: Version 3.3.9
item.description:
What's New in 3.3.9

New Features

  • Screens you added show up when you view every screen — When your device shows every screen of this Mac at once, the screens you added from that device now appear alongside this Mac's own, and your pointer reaches all of them. A Mac with no display of its own, such as a Mac mini, can now be shown this way too once you've added two or more screens to it. Turn it on with Each screen in its own window in Remio on a Mac, or with All screens at once in Remio 3.3.9 on iPhone and iPad, which is part of Remio Pro.

Improvements

  • The picture comes up about a second sooner — When you connect to control this Mac, its picture now appears about a second earlier, and your clicks and touches work from that moment instead of a moment later.
  • A still screen uses far less of your network on a direct connection — On the same Wi‑Fi or any other direct connection, Remio Host keeps a still screen at your full frame rate, and doing so used to take several megabits a second, for example for a phone or tablet used as a second display. It now sends about 0.4 Mbps in our test, so your network has far less to carry and your device far less to decode.
  • Remio uses the cable between your iPhone or iPad and this Mac — Connect an iPhone or iPad to this Mac with a USB cable and Remio now carries the session over the cable instead of Wi‑Fi: in our tests a round trip took about 1 ms over the cable against 3 to 4 ms on Wi‑Fi. Unplug the cable and the session carries on over Wi‑Fi after a pause of a few seconds; plug it back in and it returns to the cable. Needs Remio 3.3.9 on the iPhone or iPad.
  • Remio Host's window does less while a device is connected — During a session the window no longer redraws itself every second to keep its timers and numbers current. Only those readouts change, so Remio Host does less work on this Mac.

Bug Fixes

  • Fixed Remio Host freezing and restarting itself — When Remio Host adjusted its frame rate during a session, it could lock up: the picture stopped and, about ten seconds later, Remio Host restarted itself and your device had to reconnect. Changing the frame rate no longer locks it up, so the picture keeps flowing.
  • Fixed Unlock this Mac remotely not applying after a short connection drop — If the connection to Remio's server dropped for a moment during a session, Remio Host stopped following this Mac's lock for the rest of that session: when the Mac locked, keyboard and mouse from your device could still reach the lock screen with Unlock this Mac remotely turned off. The setting now applies every time this Mac locks or unlocks.

item.title: Version 3.3.8
item.description:
What's New in 3.3.8

Bug Fixes

  • Fixed Remio Host stopping to respond for a few seconds — When the app in front on this Mac was busy or still opening, tapping into it from your device or switching apps could leave Remio Host unresponsive for several seconds. Remio Host now keeps going whatever the other apps are doing.
  • Fixed short freezes when opening Remio Host's own screens — Showing the pairing QR code, opening Settings and the first-run setup could freeze Remio Host for a moment on some Macs. They now open right away.

item.title: Version 3.3.7
item.description:
What's New in 3.3.7

Improvements

  • Reconnecting is faster — Disconnect and connect again right away, and your Mac now appears in about 3 seconds instead of 5 to 6. Every other connection shows the picture a little sooner too.
  • Smooth from the very first scroll on a direct connection — On the same Wi‑Fi, or any direct connection, the picture keeps its full frame rate while this Mac's screen sits still, so the first scroll after a pause starts smooth instead of stuttering for a moment.
  • Full quality from the first second on mobile data — When a phone on 5G or 4G connects, or scrolls after this Mac's screen sat still or after its signal dropped for a moment, the picture now starts sharp and smooth right away. Before, it could start soft and choppy and take up to a minute to catch up.

Bug Fixes

  • Fixed a phone on mobile data staying on the relay — With a Direct connection port set up, a phone on 5G or 4G could still end up going through Remio's relay for the whole session, with less sharpness and smoothness than a direct connection. It now connects directly.

item.title: Version 3.3.6
item.description:
What's New in 3.3.6

Bug Fixes

  • Fixed a very blurry picture after your phone's signal dropped for a moment — On 5G, when the signal cut out for a few seconds, Remio Host could treat the gap as a slow connection: the picture turned very blurry and took up to 40 seconds to sharpen again. Now the picture comes back at full quality as soon as the signal does.

item.title: Version 3.3.5
item.description:
What's New in 3.3.5

Improvements

  • Sharper scrolling after a pause, away from home — After this Mac's screen had sat still, the next scroll from a phone on 5G or 4G, or from a laptop on another network, could start soft and take a few seconds to sharpen. It now starts sharper and keeps up better.
  • Steadier scrolling on mobile data — Scrolling from a device on 5G or 4G could creep and then jump, because your touches reached this Mac in clumps. Remio Host now evens them out, holding a touch for 20 ms at most. It steps in only when the connection needs it, so a steady connection feels exactly as before.

Bug Fixes

  • Fixed Remio Host getting stuck after you silence this Mac's speakers — If this Mac hadn't yet allowed Remio Host to record system sound, silencing its speakers or choosing a sound output from your device left Remio Host waiting for someone at the Mac to click Allow. After you left, reconnecting could fail for about a minute. Remio Host now carries on meanwhile, your device keeps hearing the sound, and the setting switches itself off if the Mac never allows it.
  • Fixed clicks pulling your aim in mouse-look games — With Lock mouse on, a click or a shot sent the pointer back to where your device's pointer was parked, so every shot yanked the camera. Clicks now land where you're aiming.
  • Fixed a display you added coming back as a new one — A display you added from the Displays panel was rebuilt for your next session as a brand-new display, so after a reconnect your device couldn't find the one you had picked and stayed on this Mac's own screen. It now comes back as the same display. Remio on iPhone and iPad takes you back to it from 3.3.5.

item.title: Version 3.3.4
item.description:
What's New in 3.3.4

Improvements

  • Your device keeps up on every network — On 5G, 4G, a busy Wi‑Fi or through the relay, a scroll could trail what you did by a third of a second to well over half a second. It now stays within about a tenth of a second on these connections, at a smooth frame rate.
  • Quicker response on your home network — What you click or type on this Mac shows up on your device around 15 ms sooner, about a third faster than before.

Bug Fixes

  • Fixed a blurry, stuttering picture on mobile data and through the relay — Since 3.3.2, scrolling on 5G, 4G or through the relay could leave the picture at a fraction of its sharpness for the rest of the session, or slow it to a few frames a second. Text now stays sharp and motion stays smooth.
  • Fixed the picture taking up to a second to come back after a short drop — When the connection blipped while this Mac's screen was still, the picture could stay frozen for up to a second after the connection recovered. It now comes back right away.
  • Fixed blurry, slow scrolling after the screen sat still on Wi-Fi — On Wi-Fi, after this Mac's screen had stayed still for a while, the next scroll could look blurry and lag for the rest of the session. Scrolling now stays sharp and quick however long the screen was still.
  • Fixed the picture freezing on mobile data — When you connected from a phone on 5G or 4G, the picture could freeze for seconds after every short drop in the connection, or stop and not come back. Remio Host now sends a picture the connection can carry, so it comes back within a moment after a drop.

item.title: Version 3.3.3
item.description:
What's New in 3.3.3

Bug Fixes

  • Fixed blurry, slow scrolling after the screen sat still on Wi-Fi — On Wi-Fi, after this Mac's screen had stayed still for a while, the next scroll could look blurry and lag for the rest of the session. Scrolling now stays sharp and quick however long the screen was still.
  • Fixed the picture freezing on mobile data — When you connected from a phone on 5G or 4G, the picture could freeze for seconds after every short drop in the connection, or stop and not come back. Remio Host now sends a picture the connection can carry, so it comes back within a moment after a drop.
  • Fixed the picture running behind on slow connections — Through the relay, on mobile data or on a busy Wi-Fi, what you saw could lag one to two seconds behind what you did. Remio Host now always sends the newest picture instead of letting older ones pile up, so the screen keeps up with you.

item.title: Version 3.3.2
item.description:
What's New in 3.3.2

Bug Fixes

  • Fixed the picture freezing on mobile data — When you connected from a phone on 5G or 4G, the picture could freeze for seconds after every short drop in the connection, or stop and not come back. Remio Host now sends a picture the connection can carry, so it comes back within a moment after a drop.
  • Fixed the picture running behind on slow connections — Through the relay, on mobile data or on a busy Wi-Fi, what you saw could lag one to two seconds behind what you did. Remio Host now always sends the newest picture instead of letting older ones pile up, so the screen keeps up with you.

item.title: Version 3.3.1
item.description:
What's New in 3.3.1

Improvements

  • Your device waits while this Mac gets its screen ready — If this Mac was slow to start sharing its screen when you connected, for example right after it woke up, your device gave up and said there was no picture. It now shows that the picture is on its way and waits while Remio Host tries again.

Bug Fixes

  • Fixed a black screen on networks slower than they looked — When a device connected directly over a weak Wi-Fi or a long-distance connection, the session could stay black or start with a frozen picture. Remio Host now notices the slow path and sends a picture that fits it.
  • Fixed a phone held upright getting this Mac's own screen — Connecting from a phone held upright could show this Mac's own screen instead of a screen sized for the phone. You now get the screen made for your phone.
  • Fixed pinch to zoom zooming much too far — Pinching from an iPhone, iPad, Android device or Windows PC zoomed far more than your fingers moved. One pinch now zooms by as much as you pinch.
  • Fixed adding a second display while this Mac's screen was asleep — If this Mac's screen had gone to sleep, using your device as a second display was refused as if the Mac had no screen. Remio Host now wakes the screen and adds the display.
  • Fixed this Mac needing a restart after a session got stuck — When macOS failed to remove the screen of a session that had ended, the next connection could show nothing until this Mac was restarted. The next session now shows this Mac's own screen, and Remio Host restarts itself to clear the stuck screen once no one is connected.
  • Fixed this Mac's screen turning on after an automatic update — When Remio Host updated itself while this Mac's screen was asleep, it could turn the screen on. It now leaves the screen as it was.
  • Fixed Remio Host staying offline after an update or restart — If the connection server was slow to answer when Remio Host started, it could give up and stay unreachable for a while before trying again. It now keeps waiting until the server answers.
  • Fixed the wrong codec showing on this Mac — During a session, Remio Host could show H.265 while the picture was sent as H.264. It now shows the codec in use.

item.title: Version 3.3.0
item.description:
What's New in 3.3.0

New Features

  • Each screen of this Mac in its own window — When this Mac has two or more screens of its own, turn on Each screen in its own window under Displays in Remio on the Mac you connect from. Remio reconnects, and each of this Mac's screens opens in a window of its own, in the same session. This Mac's screens stay on while you work, so anyone at the Mac can see what you're doing. Needs Remio 3.3.0 on the Mac you connect from.
  • Devices away from home connect directly — A phone on mobile data or a laptop in a hotel now more often reaches this Mac directly instead of through the slower relay. Remio Host asks your router to open a port for that connection and closes it again when the device disconnects. It's on by default and works with routers that allow it; turn it off in Settings → Security → Open a port on the router.
  • Quit an app on this Mac from your device — Right-click or long-press a running app under Apps in Remio on your iPhone, iPad or Mac and choose Quit. If the app is still open a few seconds later, for example because it's asking whether to save, you're offered Force Quit. Needs Remio 3.3.0 on that iPhone, iPad or Mac.
  • Mouse-look in games — Turn on Lock mouse in Remio on the Mac you connect from, or on an iPad with a mouse connected, and your movements turn the camera in games on this Mac that steer it with the mouse, while clicks and scrolling act where you aim. A stick set to Mouse look on the on-screen controller, or in a Keys & mouse controller profile in Remio for Windows, turns the camera too. Lock mouse needs Remio 3.3.0 on the Mac or iPad you connect from. Part of Remio Pro.

Improvements

  • Every pixel on large screens — When you view this Mac full screen from a Mac with a large screen, such as a 16-inch MacBook Pro, a 4K monitor or a 5K or 6K display, Remio Host used to make the picture smaller before sending it. It now sends it at that screen's full resolution, so small text is crisper. If this Mac can't keep up, Remio Host steps down to a slightly smaller picture on its own.
  • Text sharpens by itself once the screen settles — After you open a page, switch apps or stop scrolling, the first picture could stay a little soft until something on screen moved again. Remio Host now refines a still screen a moment later, on second displays too, so text gets sharper without you touching anything.
  • The pairing code changes once it's used — As soon as a device pairs with this Mac, Remio Host replaces the code and QR code on screen, so a code someone else saw can't be used to pair another device. Devices you've already paired stay paired.
  • See whether a delay comes from this Mac or the network — During a session from your iPhone, iPad or Mac, the stats overlay and Info now show Host processing: how long this Mac takes to get each picture ready to send, not counting the network. Needs Remio 3.3.0 on that iPhone, iPad or Mac.

Bug Fixes

  • Fixed sessions not connecting on some networks — Some routers, internet providers and office networks drop traffic marked as high priority, so a session could fail to connect or connect without a picture. Remio Host no longer marks its traffic this way, and neither does Remio 3.3.0 on iPhone, iPad and Mac, so sessions between them now connect on those networks.
  • Fixed Reopen Remio leaving Remio Host stuck — After you turned on a permission in System Settings and clicked Reopen Remio, during setup or on the Permissions page, Remio Host could get stuck while closing instead of opening again, and other devices couldn't reach this Mac until someone restarted it. It now closes and opens again by itself.
  • Fixed devices losing Wake Up for this Mac — If Remio Host couldn't read this Mac's network address when it started, your other devices lost the address they use to wake it, and Wake Up stopped working. Remio Host now leaves the address they already have in place.
  • Fixed a brief connection drop locking this Mac — With Lock when session ends turned on, a device that only lost its connection, for example when Wi-Fi drops or you switch networks, now has 30 seconds to reconnect and finds your Mac as it left it instead of at the lock screen. If no device comes back, the Mac still locks, and disconnecting from your device still locks it right away.
  • Fixed Caps Lock typing lower-case letters — With Caps Lock on, typing from the Windows PC or Mac you connect from gave lower-case letters on this Mac. It now types capitals. From a Mac this needs Remio 3.3.0 on that Mac, which also follows a Caps Lock that was already on when you connected or that you switched in another app.
  • Fixed Shift-click and Ctrl-click from a Windows PC — Clicking while holding Shift, Ctrl or Alt on a Windows PC now reaches this Mac with the key held, instead of as a plain click. Shift-click selects a range. With Swap Ctrl / Cmd on in Remio for Windows, as it is unless you changed it, Ctrl-click works like ⌘-click, for example to add to a selection or open a link in a new tab.
  • Fixed keys that didn't reach this Mac — From another Mac, some keys were ignored or only typed their character: the extra key on UK and European keyboards, the Japanese keyboard's ¥, ろ, keypad comma, 英数 and かな keys, F16 to F20, and the number pad's = key. They now arrive as real keys, so they also work in shortcuts and password fields.
  • Fixed scrolling the wrong window from an iPad — If you scrolled or pinched to zoom from an iPad before moving the pointer, the pointer on this Mac could jump to the top-left corner of the screen and scroll whatever was there. It now acts on what's under the pointer.
  • Fixed sound stopping when the chosen speaker goes away — If the speaker you picked under Sound output left this Mac during a session, such as AirPods disconnecting or a USB speaker being unplugged, your device went quiet. Remio Host now carries on with whatever this Mac is playing through.
  • Fixed colors looking slightly off in a small window — When you viewed this Mac in a small window or at a low resolution, colors on your device could look slightly off. They now look the same at every size.
  • Fixed Remio Host's helper using more and more memory — The helper that starts Remio Host again if it crashes or freezes took up a little more memory the longer your Mac stayed on. It no longer keeps growing.

item.title: Version 3.2.5
item.description:
What's New in 3.2.5

Improvements

  • Sharper on 5K and 6K displays — A Mac with a 5K or 6K display, such as a Studio Display, Pro Display XDR or iMac 5K, controlling this Mac now gets full Retina sharpness instead of a lower-resolution picture. Needs the updated Remio app on that Mac.
  • Every device starts at full quality — A data limit set by one device, for example a phone on mobile data, now ends with its session. The next device no longer starts out blurry for a few seconds.
  • Direct connections stay direct — With a fixed direct-connection port set in Remio, a short network drop or another device taking over no longer leaves the session on the slower relay path. It reconnects directly within seconds.

Bug Fixes

  • "Fit to this device" follows your window — With Keep screen on, resizing the window on the controlling device now resizes the fitted display too.
  • Fixed a second display going dark after a reconnect — After a reconnect or a Remio Host restart, the old connection could take a second display down a few seconds into the new one, with "This computer can't add a second display". It now stays on.
  • Fixed Remio Host restarting on MacBooks — On a MacBook, a slow battery or charger check could make Remio Host restart itself and drop your connection. It no longer waits on it.
  • Fixed a black screen after a quick reconnect — A device that reconnected twice in quick succession could be left without a picture. The picture now comes back.
  • Fixed no picture on very large displays — On Macs that cannot encode a very large display, such as an older iMac 5K, Remio Host now steps down to a slightly smaller picture instead of showing nothing.

item.title: Version 3.2.3
item.description:
What's New in 3.2.3

Improvements

  • Clearer screen names — On your device, the screen this Mac makes for remote control now shows up as "This computer's desktop" instead of "Remio Virtual".

Bug Fixes

  • Fixed "no picture" on a second display next to remote control — When a second display joined while another device was controlling this Mac, the Mac took a few seconds to prepare the desktop without saying so, and the second display gave up with "no picture". The second display now waits, and the picture appears. The device in control also keeps its picture when it reconnects at the same moment a second display joins.
  • Back in control right away — With second displays connected, a device controlling this Mac that was closed and reopened, or lost its connection, could be refused with "Second display in use" for up to 90 seconds. It now gets straight back in.
  • Fixed reconnecting next to second displays — A device coming back to control this Mac while second displays are connected is no longer turned away or mistaken for a second display. When several second displays reconnect at the same moment, for example after Remio Host restarts, each one comes back instead of one stopping for good.
  • Fixed a second display going dark — When one device connected to control this Mac at the same moment another added a second display, the second display could go dark with "This computer can't add a second display". Both now connect.
  • A clear message when remote control ends — On a Mac with no screen of its own, when the remote-control session a second display extends comes to an end, the second display now says so instead of "This computer can't add a second display".
  • Fixed the picture not coming back — A device that connected just as another session was ending, such as the same device reconnecting within a moment, could be left without a picture. The same could happen when switching to another screen or resizing did not go through. The picture now comes back.
  • Fixed a crash when the disk is full — Remio Host could quit when the Mac ran completely out of disk space. It now keeps running.

item.title: Version 3.2.2
item.description:
What's New in 3.2.2

New Features

  • Ready for Second Display — Once your Remio app updates, your iPad, iPhone, tablet or another computer can become an extra screen for this Mac. It extends your desktop instead of copying it: your own screens stay on, you drag windows onto it like onto any other display, and it shows this Mac's pointer. Windows keep the size they have on your Mac, each device's screen comes back where you left it, and sound stays on the Mac. Everything stays on your local network.
  • Several second displays at once — Up to three devices can each add a screen of their own, even while another device is controlling this Mac. The Remio Host window and the menu bar list every device with its own Disconnect, so you can end one without touching the others. Drop a file on a device's row to send it to that device only, and text and pictures you copy on the Mac reach every device.

Improvements

  • A still screen no longer looks like a bad connection — When nothing on your screen was changing, the Host showed the connection as poor, in red. It now simply says Idle.
  • Smoother picture on busy networks — Remio Host no longer resends the whole screen every 30 seconds, which caused brief stutters on slower Wi-Fi.
  • Full frame rate after a takeover — A device that takes a session over from another now gets the full frame rate straight away, instead of the slower rate the previous device had dropped to.
  • Told at once when another device wins — When two devices try to connect to this Mac at the same moment, the one that loses now sees right away that another device took over, instead of a connection error about 15 seconds later. Needs the updated Remio apps.
  • Quitting tells your devices — When you quit Remio Host, a connected device is told right away that this Mac stopped sharing, instead of waiting for a time-out.

Bug Fixes

  • Fixed sessions ending after about an hour — A session from a signed-in device could end on its own after about an hour. Sessions now last as long as you need.
  • Fixed Remio Host restarting again and again — On some Macs, macOS's keychain could stop answering when the Host started, and the Host was restarted over and over. It now waits, keeps running, and carries on as soon as the keychain answers.
  • Fixed HDR sometimes not turning on — A device could be told HDR was on while it was still receiving the standard picture. HDR now starts with the first frame.
  • Fixed screen sharing carrying on after a device left — When a device dropped out, for example when this Mac went to sleep, a late message from it could restart screen sharing with nobody connected. It now stops together with the session.

item.title: Version 3.1.0
item.description:
What's New in 3.1.0

New Features

  • Copy images between your Mac and your devices — Copy a picture on one side and paste it on the other, in both directions. The new Clipboard section in Remio Host shows everything that crossed during the session, lets you copy any of it again, and tells you right away if something didn't arrive. Images need Remio 3.1 or later on the Mac, iPhone, iPad or Windows PC you connect from; text works with every version.
  • HDR streaming — On a Mac with Apple silicon, iPhones, iPads and Macs with an HDR screen can now see your desktop in HDR, with the brightness and color it really has. Turn on HDR in the device's stream settings.

Improvements

  • Smoother scrolling — Scrolling with a mouse wheel or trackpad now stops cleanly at the edge of a page and lands where you aimed.
  • Faster reconnects — When your Mac's network changes, Remio Host is reachable again on the new network straight away.

Bug Fixes

  • Fixed Remio Host freezing when you switched back to it — The Host could stop responding the moment you brought its window to the front. It now always responds.
  • Fixed a rare crash on a Mac that has been sharing for a long time — Remio Host could quit on its own after running for a day or more. It now keeps running.
  • Fixed a crash when VoiceOver reads the pairing code — The pairing code can now be read aloud without the Host quitting.
  • Extra displays stay put — A display you added in the middle of a session no longer disappears, and when another device takes over the session it gets your extra displays too.
  • The pointer reaches every corner — On a streamed display placed beside or above your main screen, the pointer now reaches the whole display.
  • Empty files can be sent — Sending an empty file to or from your Mac now works instead of failing.

item.title: Version 3.0.8
item.description:
What's New in 3.0.8

  • Remio Host keeps itself up to date — New versions now download in the background and install on their own while no device is connected, so a Mac you reach from far away stays current without anyone sitting at it. Turn it off any time in Settings → Install updates automatically.
  • A required update no longer takes your Mac offline — When an update was required, the Host stopped sharing until it was installed, and on many Macs it waited for someone to click a button on the Mac itself. It now keeps sharing and installs the update at the next quiet moment.
  • Fixed "it says it updated, then asks to update again" — If you installed a new version from the website while Remio Host was running, the Host kept running the old version and kept asking for the update. It now switches to the new version by itself.
  • A MacBook with its lid closed shows the picture — A MacBook on power with its lid closed could accept your connection and then show nothing. It now wakes itself up for you and streams.
  • A lid-closed MacBook keeps its external display — With the lid closed and one external display attached, every other session could leave that display switched off afterwards, and the Mac would go to sleep. Your display now comes back exactly as it was.

item.title: Version 3.0.7
item.description:
What's New in 3.0.7

Bug Fixes

  • Connecting from a phone or tablet no longer ends in "reopen Remio" — On some Macs, the display the Host creates for your phone or tablet didn't come up, and the Host took that for a missing permission: it stopped sharing and told you to reopen Remio, even while another device was streaming from the same Mac without trouble. It now tries that display again and, if it still doesn't appear, streams your Mac's own screen instead — sharing stays on.
  • Files you send to your Mac show up where you can see them — Since 3.0, a file the Host received only raised a notification, easy to miss when you're looking at the Mac through Remio. The Host now shows the file in a Finder window on the screen you're viewing, as it did before 3.0.

Improvements

  • A sharper picture on 120 Hz screens when your Mac is at its limit — When your Mac couldn't keep up with a large 120 Hz screen, such as an iPad Pro 13", the Host kept 120 fps and lowered the resolution, so text looked soft. It now steps down to 60 fps first — still smooth — and lowers the resolution only if 60 fps is too much as well. Over a relay connection a Mac at its limit now holds 60 fps too, instead of letting the frame rate fall.

item.title: Version 3.0.6
item.description:
What's New in 3.0.6

Bug Fixes

  • Detailed scenes no longer freeze the picture — Opening a large photo or cutting to a busy new scene at high resolution could freeze the stream for about three seconds, with nothing to say why. Every frame the Host sends now arrives in one piece, so the picture keeps moving.
  • Text-heavy screens keep their full frame rate — On a large screen full of text, the stream could quietly settle at half its frame rate. It now holds the full rate.
  • The Host picks itself up if the Mac's video encoder hangs — Rarely, macOS's video encoder stops answering. The Host then still showed as online, but no device could connect, sometimes for hours. It now notices within seconds and restarts itself.
  • No more unexpected restarts — The Host could restart itself every few minutes in three cases: on a Mac mini after a session ended, while the "You're up to date" message was left on screen, and while macOS was waiting for permission to use the Host's saved key. None of these restart it any more.

Improvements

  • Full sharpness at 120 Hz on big screens — On large, high-refresh sessions the Host used to lower the resolution and fall back to 60 fps to keep up. It now keeps full resolution at 120 fps, and returns to full sharpness sooner after a busy moment.
  • 120 Hz sessions start at full quality — A 120 Hz session on your local network started at half the quality your connection could carry, and was capped below the limit you set. It now starts at the right quality and uses your limit.

item.title: Version 3.0.5
item.description:
What's New in 3.0.5

Bug Fixes

  • Fast motion no longer falls behind — Scrolling a long page, playing a video or anything else that changes the whole screen could leave the picture, and every click and keystroke with it, more than a second behind on a local network. The Host now sends each frame as soon as it is ready, so what you do shows up right away — even at 120 Hz.
  • The Host uses your cable again — On a Mac connected by both a cable and Wi‑Fi, the stream could run over Wi‑Fi. It now picks the wired connection, for a steadier picture with less delay.

item.title: Version 3.0.4
item.description:
What's New in 3.0.4

Bug Fixes

  • Turning on screen sharing is noticed straight away — A Mac where you had switched Remio Host on under System Settings → Privacy & Security → Remote Desktop could stay on "Waiting for you" for good, however many times you pressed Recheck, reopened Remio or reinstalled it. The Host now sees the switch within seconds, and a Mac that was stuck this way starts sharing as soon as it updates — nothing to grant again.
  • No more detour to the wrong settings page — Right after the first permission prompt, macOS could show a second one whose button opened Screen & System Audio Recording instead of Remote Desktop. That second prompt no longer appears, and every button in Remio takes you straight to Remote Desktop. If you already turned Remio Host on under Screen & System Audio Recording, that works too — leave it as it is.

Improvements

  • A Mac you leave on stays reachable — If the Host ever crashes or freezes while you're away, it now starts again by itself: within seconds after a crash, a little over a minute after a freeze. Quitting Remio yourself still quits it. The helper that does this shows up as a background item from Remio Host in System Settings → General → Login Items; switching it off there turns it off.
  • Back online by itself after long sleeps — After the Mac had been asleep for more than an hour, or its clock had drifted, the Host could be turned away by the connection server and stay offline until someone restarted it. It now reconnects on its own, and keeps retrying while the network is down instead of waiting for a change it might never notice.
  • Screen sharing keeps coming back — When macOS cuts the screen capture and the first retries fail, the Host now keeps trying every ten minutes for as long as it takes, instead of giving up and waiting for someone at the Mac.

item.title: Version 3.0.3
item.description:
What's New in 3.0.3

  • The Host window's sidebar is back on macOS Sequoia — on macOS 15 the sidebar opened with its rows pushed up under the window buttons and the rest of the column empty, so there was no way to reach Connect, File sharing, Accessories, Devices or Permissions. The full list of pages is back.
  • A display set to "Fit to this device" now actually follows it — switching a virtual display to follow the device viewing it could come back refused, leaving it at the fixed size it already had.

item.title: Version 3.0.2
item.description:
What's New in 3.0.2

Bug Fixes

  • A Mac that stopped sharing because the screen capture broke now starts sharing again on its own — If macOS cut the capture mid-session and the automatic retries could not bring it back, the Host used to switch sharing off and wait for someone to press Start on the Mac. It now comes back by itself after a few seconds (waiting longer if it keeps happening), and only asks for a hand when the capture is genuinely broken.
  • Devices no longer see the Mac as online when it has stopped sharing — After that kind of stop, the Host kept telling the server it still had its old room, so every device saw the Mac online, and every connect failed with "no active host" until the Host was restarted. The Host now drops the room the moment it stops, and corrects itself if the server ever reports the room gone while it is idle.
  • The Host window is dark on every Mac, whatever the Mac itself is set to — On a Mac set to Light appearance the window's own frame stayed light around a dark page: the sidebar came up pale with white text on it, and a grey band sat across the top of the window. The sidebar, the title bar and every sheet and alert are now dark, the way the rest of the app already was.
  • A Mac that once took a required update is offered ordinary updates again — After a required update had installed itself, the Host went on quietly downloading later releases in the background instead of telling you about them — and since a Mac you leave on is rarely quit, those releases never finished installing. It asks again before installing, and now looks for a new version every hour.

item.title: Version 3.0.1
item.description:
What's New in 3.0.1

Bug Fixes

  • Fixed the Host window on macOS Sequoia — On macOS 15 the sidebar opened with a single row tucked under the window buttons and the rest of the column empty, so there was no way to reach Connect, File sharing, Accessories, Devices or Permissions. The full list of pages is back, and the window now opens the same way on every version of macOS.

item.title: Version 3.0.0
item.description:
What's New in 3.0.0

New Features

  • A new Host window — Remio Host now looks and behaves like System Settings: a sidebar with Connect, File sharing, Accessories, Devices, Permissions and Settings, and a real screen behind each one. Everything used to be floating panels stacked over a QR code, appearing and disappearing on their own; now each thing has a place you can go back to. The window also keeps the height you drag it to.
  • Send and receive files — The File sharing page sends files to the device you're connected from and receives files sent back the other way. Every transfer keeps a line in the history under the name of the device it came from or went to, so you can open a file you were sent last week in Finder, or send the same file again to the same device with one click.
  • A file arriving while your Mac is locked waits for you — If your Mac locks in the middle of an incoming file, the transfer pauses with a countdown instead of quietly writing to your disk while nobody is at the keyboard, and picks up exactly where it left off when you unlock.
  • A Devices page that tells you where access came from — Your devices are now grouped by how they got in: paired with a code on this Mac, or trusted because they're signed in to your account. Open any of them to see what it actually is — model, system, app version, screen, how it connects — give it a name of your own, or take its access away.
  • Two different ways to take access away — Block from this Mac keeps the device on your account but stops it reaching this computer. Remove from account signs it out everywhere. The buttons now say which one you're about to do, instead of one Remove that quietly did more than it looked like.
  • A log of what happened with your devices — The last 30 days of pairings, refused attempts, wrong PINs, session takeovers and revocations, in plain language, per device and across the Mac. A badge appears on Devices when something worth looking at happened while you weren't watching.
  • A Permissions page that's always there — Permissions used to be a panel that only appeared when something was broken, which is exactly when it's too late to find it. It's now a permanent place in the sidebar showing what each permission is for and what state it's in. When a macOS update quietly stops a permission from working, the page says so and tells you to switch it off and back on — rather than sending you to press Allow on something that's already allowed. Granting a permission in System Settings is noticed within seconds; you don't have to restart Remio or come back to the window.
  • Your pairing code expires — The six-digit code now lasts five minutes, with the countdown on screen, and rotates itself. Five wrong attempts replace it immediately and tell you it happened. A code left on screen all afternoon was a code anyone on the network could keep guessing at.
  • Choose whether your own devices skip pairing — Settings has a switch for letting devices signed in to your account connect without a code. On by default.

Improvements

  • Connecting is quicker — Setting up the display on the way into a session dropped from 1.69 to 0.76 seconds, which is time your device spends on "Connecting…" before the first frame.
  • The session panel says what the connection is actually doing — Packet loss, jitter and how many times the picture froze now sit alongside bitrate and latency, so a session that feels wrong can be pointed at something.
  • When a second device takes over, the window says so — Handing a session to another device now names the device that took it, marks it as the new owner and restarts the session clock, instead of silently swapping who is in control.
  • Disconnecting a device no longer looks like unpairing it — Pressing Disconnect told the device it was "no longer paired", which made it look like it had lost access for good. It now says this Mac ended the session, and the device can simply connect again.
  • One name for each permission, on every screen — "Screen sharing" and "Mouse and keyboard control" are called that everywhere in Remio. Apple's own names appear only inside the step-by-step instructions, word for word as macOS writes them, so what you read here matches what you're looking for over there.

Bug Fixes

  • Fixed a Mac with both Ethernet and Wi‑Fi on hosting over Wi‑Fi — When a cable and Wi‑Fi were both connected, the host could offer its Wi‑Fi address first and every client would stream through it. The wired connection now takes precedence.
  • Fixed your monitors coming back in the wrong order — A display arranged to the left of your main one came back on the right after a session, and any vertical offset was lost, leaving your mouse crossing between screens in the wrong direction until you fixed it by hand. Remio now records where every display actually sits and puts them back exactly.
  • Fixed a left click opening the right-click menu — After using any shortcut with Control, every click that followed behaved as a Control-click for the rest of the session, so left-clicking opened context menus.
  • Fixed copying on your device and pasting on the Mac giving you the old text — Copying something on the device you're controlling from and pressing ⌘V on the Mac could paste the previous thing, or nothing at all, and the workaround was pasting into another app and copying again. Every copy now lands. Your Mac's clipboard is also no longer replaced by the device's the moment you connect.
  • Fixed the Host freezing seconds after a device connects — On a Mac signed in to the same iCloud account as another Apple device, something copied on that other device could stop the Host dead as it tried to fetch the content over the network.
  • Fixed the Host quitting when a device offered an impossible file — A single message claiming a file size that couldn't exist took the whole Host down, session included. Oversized files are refused with a message now.
  • Fixed the window getting shorter every time you opened it — The window lost about fifty points of height per launch — 658, then 606, then 554 — and forgot whatever height you had set for it.
  • Fixed reconnecting from the same device resetting the session clock — A brief network drop restarted the timer as if a new device had arrived, and numbers from the previous connection could be shown under the new device's name.
  • Fixed a failed transfer you couldn't do anything about — A transfer that failed left a row in the history with no way to retry it or pick a different file.
  • Fixed small files showing as "0 KB" — Anything under a kilobyte reported itself as empty while it transferred perfectly well.
